title: Future plans, Social Security and the Hall's other musicians
summary: Talk of retirement and of fellow Hall piano players, the old age of the musicians, few gigs left and small pension income.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What kind of plans you got for the future, if any?
You're going to buy me a house and sit down.
You're going to buy me a house and sit down and collect your Social Security, huh? That's right. You got a little way to go yet, though, huh? No, I don't have that many years to go.
What, let's see, 13? How old are you now?
I'm 58. 58. Well, you got four more years. I'll be naked.
Yeah.
Remember what we were talking about earlier, but— I'll be back. I'll be back.
You'll be back.
Yeah, you'll be back. Yeah, you'll be back.
Yeah, you'll be back. Yeah, you'll be back.

Yeah, we were talking about Dave Oxley when he carried him off in the ambulance. I'll be back, I'll be back. Well, remember we were talking a little while ago about mentioning about Cap, and talking about all the different people, all the musicians who have died, and they've all been playing at Preservation Hall at one time or another. And—
One time somebody dies, somebody said they need a piano player up there. I said, you got two or three of them up there already, don't need me.
Yeah, what other piano players who played at Preservation Hall at the time?
Well, I played back, he played there. I played there.
Sunday. Sunday, you go play there.
Well, Sunday I played more at Dixieland though, didn't I?
Yeah, but he played there. Yeah. I couldn't have that much, but he played there.
But you know, that is kind of strange, aren't you? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
many piano players.
Most of them are all the musicians. Well you see, what happened most to all the four musicians is the one that played at the reservation.

That has a lot to do with it because so many of the musicians who just weren't doing anything and then started playing at the hall, and most of them are up in age, and some of them were sick like Joe Watkins, he had that stroke, and then there isn't much anymore to do. If you can't walk in a parade you just don't play, and there aren't that many gigs around anymore.
Preservation of Holland and Dixonite.
Preservation of Holland and Dixonite, and that's it. Only two. That's all that's left, unless you get a tour. Not too many of those.
I've been fortunate most every year.
You've been lucky about that. That brought you through to your Social Security. Now you get your what, $68?
$68 a month. Fingin' on a raise. You're gonna need it. Well it's a fool to put that up there at one double O. Yeah.
Well that will leave Sheik some money over. He has to take a cab home every night when he stays out like things are so bad and where he lives.
I'm $62 a month. Just on cab? Just cab. Now I come on the bus, I catch the bus in the evening coming.
Well that takes care of the other age for you. Yeah. They keep raising the bus fare, it'll be cheaper to take a cab both ways.
Yeah, bus fare and cab fare, that eats up my pension.
